summary.text: Chris Jones is the Democratic nominee for Arkansas's 2nd Congressional District. A physicist and ordained minister who grew up in Pine Bluff, he led the Arkansas Regional Innovation Hub before becoming the 2022 Democratic nominee for governor, a race he lost to Sarah Huckabee Sanders. He is running on lowering costs, healthcare access, economic opportunity and voting rights.

paragraphs.text: Jones was born in Pine Bluff, Arkansas, the son of two preachers, and graduated from Watson Chapel High School.

He earned a B.S. in physics and mathematics from Morehouse College in 1999, which he says he attended on a full NASA scholarship, an M.S. in nuclear engineering/technology and policy from MIT in 2003, and a Ph.D. in urban planning from MIT in 2016.
His career includes work as a nuclear engineer, physicist, minister and nonprofit leader, and he describes himself as an ordained minister.

He says he returned to Arkansas to serve as executive director of the Arkansas Regional Innovation Hub, which he led for three years, working on entrepreneurship, STEAM education and workforce training.
Jones won the May 24, 2022 Democratic primary for Arkansas governor over four opponents, then lost the general election to Republican Sarah Huckabee Sanders, 63% to 35%.
He announced his campaign for the 2nd District on October 9, 2025, and won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary over Zack Huffman.
Jones says he is married to a combat veteran and is the father of three girls.
